issues.detail: The Greek 'εις το εθνος μου' means 'to my nation/people' (i.e., the Jewish nation), but the Vietnamese says 'cho dân ngoại của tôi' which means 'for my Gentile people/nation' — this reverses the meaning, making it sound like the Gentiles are the recipients, whereas the Greek clearly refers to the speaker's own nation (Israel).
